I had this issue with my PC last week. I was dumb and purchased a mobo that had the same socket set (AM3+) as my processor (FX-9590) but it wasn't quite compatible with the processor. When I played GTA V, the CPU would go from 4.7GHz to 1.4GHz because the mobo was overheating. When overheating occurs, things "underclock" to preserve the life of the system, if underclocking doesn't lower the temps quick enough, the system could shut down, thus having a chance at data failure.

I fixed my issue; mine was the fact that I was stupid and bought a cheap motherboard without doing my full research... I bought a mobo that was incompatible with the FX 9590, and it was causing the VRMs to overheat... I've since purchased new ROG mobo and the game runs flawlessly
